title: Harmonize cross-encoder variants and regression guardrails for rerank endpoint
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: This ticket coordinates selection, validation, and rollout guardrails for cross-encoder variants used by the reranking endpoint. The goal is to offer multiple ranked model variants (quality-first, latency-balanced, compact-ML-multilingual) with deterministic upgrade paths and automated regression detection so product teams can safely upgrade without unexpected quality or latency regressions.
problem_statement: We have several cross-encoder families evaluated separately (compact vs full, quantized vs FP16, language-specialized vs pan-lingual). Customers are requesting higher-quality multilingual reranking while SLOs limit P95 latency and cost. Previous upgrades caused subtle quality regressions on non-English queries and cache-incompatibilities across embeddings. We need a repeatable process to pick variants, calibrate scores across models, and automate regression checks before rollout.
proposal: 1) Define three canonical rerank variants to productize: quality-max (high compute, best MRR/nDCG), balanced (lower latency, near-quality), compact-multilingual (quantized, supports >20 languages). 2) Build a unified evaluation harness that runs offline datasets (English+15 non-English corpora) and measures MRR, nDCG@10, top1 accuracy, plus latency P50/P95 and GPU memory. 3) Add score calibration layer to normalize logits between models so downstream thresholds remain stable. 4) Integrate the harness into CI and the console release pipeline: any candidate model must pass quality/regression gates and latency/cost budgets before canary. 5) Implement staged rollout with traffic allocation, automatic rollback triggers, and telemetry dashboards for fast detection.
acceptance_criteria: Three variant builds (quality-max, balanced, compact-multilingual) published to model catalog with metadata and performance profiles
Evaluation harness added to rerank CI that runs full multilingual corpus and emits metrics within 2 hours
Score calibration implemented such that average top1 score delta between current and candidate is < 0.02 after calibration
Automated regression gates: if MRR drop >0.5% on any language test set or P95 latency increases >15% for balanced/compact variants, block rollout
Canary rollout playbook updated in Console with rollback automation and alert runbooks
technical_notes:
- Candidate families: ce-large-fp16, ce-large-int8, ce-medium-fp16, ce-compact-quant. Quantized models require runtime kernel toggles and memory pinning.
- Calibration approach: collect scores on holdout set, fit per-model affine transform (scale+bias) per-language cluster, persist calibration table. Keep calibration lightweight to execute at startup or as background job.
- Latency targets: balanced P95 <= 220ms for 128-token pairs on NVidia A10x, compact P95 <= 120ms. Quality-max allowed up to 400ms P95.
- Regression harness artifacts saved to S3 with standardized schema for comparison; attach to PRs and console release.
- Ensure embedding compatibility: validate that embedding model + reranker pair maintain relative ordering. Add embedding-pairing test vectors.
- Autoscaling: adjust target batch sizes per variant; compact can be batched larger. Update autoscaler policy templates for variant-aware scaling.
- Backwards compatibility: if model variant removes output fields, fail the model catalog upload.
- Security: model artifacts scanned via existing signing pipeline.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal validation — run harness on internal corpora and hand-labeled sets (2 weeks)
Stage 2: CI gating — require green on regression harness for pull requests; attach results to PRs
Stage 3: Canary — 2% traffic for 24h, monitor MRR/nDCG by language, latency P50/P95, error rates
Stage 4: Progressive ramp — 10% for 48h, 50% for 24h, then 100% if no alerts
Rollback triggers: MRR drop >0.5% on any language OR latency P95 increase >15% OR error rate spike >3x baseline
test_plan: Offline: multilingual test suite (EN, ES, FR, DE, ZH, JA, KO, PT, RU, AR, HI, TR, VI, ID, PL)
Synthetic stress: high-concurrency synthetic traffic to measure batching effects and GPU memory behavior
A/B experiments: run balanced vs quality-max for 2 weeks on subset of customers and collect downstream CTR/engagement signals
Human eval: sample 1k rerank outputs per language and collect pairwise preference judgments from annotators
CI integration: post-merge job that runs on new model artifacts and uploads a regression report
